question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹60, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, Principal (P) = (SI for 1 year)² ÷ (CI − SI)

⇒ SI for 1 year = ₹40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ CI − SI = ₹60 − ₹40 = ₹20

⇒ P = 20² ÷ 20 = 400 ÷ 20 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹40

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹60

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ 2

Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = Interest on 1st year's SI

Rate (R) = (Difference ÷ SI for 1 year) × 100

Principal (P) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ (R × 1)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) = 60 − 40 = ₹20

⇒ The difference is simply the interest earned on the 1st year's SI.

⇒ Rate (R) = (20 ÷ 20) × 100 = 100%

⇒ Using the formula for SI: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = (P × 100 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = P

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain principal can be directly calculated as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated strictly on the original principal amount for each period. Thus, SI remains constant for every year: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. In the first year, CI and SI are always equal.
